definitions.gloss: hanafuda; flower cards; Japanese playing cards
definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese card game using a deck of 48 cards divided into 12 suits, each representing a month of the year and its associated flower or plant.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}に{花札|はなふだ}のルールを{教|おし}えてもらった。
examples.english: My grandfather taught me the rules of hanafuda.

examples.japanese: {正月|しょうがつ}に{家族|かぞく}で{花札|はなふだ}をするのが{毎年|まいとし}の{楽|たの}しみだ。
examples.english: Playing hanafuda with the family at New Year's is something I look forward to every year.

notes:
A compound of {花|はな} (flower) and {札|ふだ} (card/tag). The 48-card deck has 12 suits corresponding to the months, each featuring seasonal plants: January ({松|まつ}, pine), February ({梅|うめ}, plum), March ({桜|さくら}, cherry), and so on through December.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {花札|はなふだ}で{遊|あそ}ぶ: to play hanafuda
- {花札|はなふだ}の{絵柄|えがら}: hanafuda card designs
- {花札|はなふだ}を{配|くば}る: to deal hanafuda cards

CULTURAL NOTE:
Hanafuda has been played in Japan since the Edo period and remains popular as a family game, especially during {正月|しょうがつ} (New Year). The game company Nintendo originally began as a hanafuda manufacturer in 1889. Common game variants include こいこい and {花合|はなあ}わせ.
